newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGIP offers to buy Cerus' Valeo stake.
newsitem.headline: CGIP offers to buy Cerus' Valeo stake.

text.p: French holding group CGIP said on Thursday that it wanted to complete negotiations to buy Cerus's stake in car part maker Valeo.

CGIP also said in a statement that its board had authorised the offer for sale of almost half of its stake in U.S. packaging giant Crown Cork and Seal, but it would remain that company's largest shareholder, with 10 pct of the stock.

The statement confirmed reports that CGIP, encouraged by the French government and car manufacturers, was negotiating to acquire the 28 percent stake in Valeo put up for sale by Cerus, Italian financier Carlo De Benedetti's French holding company.
CGIP earlier this month denied it was planning to launch takeover bids for either Cerus or Valeo.
"(The board) expressed the wish that the discussions relating to the acquisiton of Cerus's holding in Valeo be completed," the CGIP statement.

"Within this framework, the board authroised the offer for sale of almost half of CGIP's holding in Crowm Cork and Seal, the world's largest packaging company. With 10 percent of the stock, CGIP would remain its largest shareholder without any modification of the existing agreements," it said.

The statement added that Crown Cork and Seal had announced on Thursday that it was proceeding with preliminary formalities required by U.S. stock exchnage authorities for such an offering expected to occur in late October.
The company did not dislose terms either of its offer to Cerus or of its proposed sale of the Crown Cork and Seal stake.
Analysts have said Cerus's holding in Valeo is worth more than five billion francs at current market prices.
Under French bourse rules, the purchase of less than 33 pct of a company's share capital does not require a public takeover offer.
